# Spiritual Translation of the Chapter

---

** ¶2. ** After the Divine Truth proce eding from the Lord had established the ordered states of the mind at every degree , it descended and made itself present within the natural mind. It communicated its intention to the Divine Love in operation , which set in motion the thre efold cycle of spiritual influx and caused these living progress ions to extend above every elevated state of good. The Divine Love breath ed spiritual understanding into these states , vivified them, stir red them into activity, and pur ified the natural mind with tru ths. Now the resid ual imp urities that had accumulated within the three containing forms of the mind — the form that had held corru pted truth, the form that had held sh eer ignorance, and the form that had held self-love — all that had been discharged into the natural mind was gathered up and deposited into the general reservoir of sensory knowledge, bounded within its own walls and vessels. This is why the body of natural -sensory knowledge is bitter and bar ren: it has received its corruption and its har shness from the cle ansing and purging of those three containing forms of the mind.

---

**¶3.** When the Divine Source of all life arose , ascending by withdrawal into the most interior states, He pur ified the entire cycle of knowledges in the mind , washing away and loos ening every sed iment of fals ity that had settled within it . He cast these impurities down ward into the great interior reservoir of sensory knowledge, as from a height . And those residues — the dre gs of the pur ification of the cycle of knowing — He let fall and mixed them into the body of sens ory knowledge below . The inher ent form ative principle within that knowledge drew these resid ues together of its own nature ; and this organizing thought gathered the waste into a consolidated mass and fixed it into a settled and end uring form.

---

** ¶4.** Upon this self hood formed within the sens ory mind was stam ped the imprint of every temporal progression of spiritual life — the impression of its smallest moments and its hours , of its days and months and years, the form of every particular knowledge and of the complete cycle of spiritual states. It came into existence out of all these and was precip itated from their collective power into the reservoir of sensory life . Every image and seal , every aspect and doctrine and deliber ation belonging to the whole ordered arrangement of the mind — all these were impressed upon this selfhood, because it is the final residue of them all. Therefore , every knowledge that shines forth and every state of the mind that revol ves in its cycle finds in this prop rium either its prov ocation or its confirmation.

---

**¶5.** This selfhood was precip itated into the sensory mind in the manner that truth , obsc ured into a cloud, might release itself down ward into a body of natural knowing. It was compelled wholly down ward by the operation of Divine power and the governance of the higher faculties of heaven . It was swept to the form ative ground — the place established for its construction in the original ordering of the whole mind — and the sensory mind itself received and conceived it, becoming its chief sculptor and chief sh aper. The sens ory mind formed this proprium into a distinct lik eness, transform ing it more thoroughly than any other residue within the natural mind.

---

**¶ 6.** This process is comparable to a form ative power that might take the distinct impressions of inn umerable separate knowledges, subject them all to the fire of one ruling love, and m elt them down into a single image . A thousand separate forms of knowledge and a thousand distinct shapes of affection are thus f used and perf ected into one consolidated self hood.

---

**¶ 7.** So it is with this selfhood dwelling in the sensory mind: it was mol ded and scul pted by the dominant power of self-love operating within it, drawn from the many teachings, deliber ations, and counsels that constitute the lowest resid ue of the mind 's entire cycle of states.

---

**¶8. ** This arche typal self hood was permitted to take form for three purposes.

---

**¶9.** * The first: * That the whole revol ving cycle of mental states might be relieved and purified of the burden of fals ity within it. In the same way that the ten degrees of the interior mind were purified and relieved of the burden contained in the three vessels of corru pted truth, ignor ance, and self-love, so too was it done to the ou termost cycle of natural knowing — that it also might be unb urdened and cle ansed of the waste and imp urity lod ged within it.

---

** ¶10.** *The second :* That the selfhood might serve as a fetter and a prison upon the revol ving cycle of natural knowledge and the states that are bound to it. When the fals ities and di sor dered aff ections of the natural mind wish to ascend into the higher states of the mind, the weight of the proprium drags them back as with a chain of natural truth , and they are unable to rise . And when the powers of natural knowing conspire toward some deception and it enters their deliber ation to descend into the external mind to act, they are unable to descend because of this fixed stake that is driven into the cycle at the very foundation of the heavenly degrees . This is the one restra int. But there is another: the sleepless guardians — the vigil ant provisions of Divine order — are set over the cycle , and by them it is turned perpetually and never comes to rest in any single state of fals ity.

---

**¶ 11.** *The third:* That the spiritual understanding , the truth, and the love which g ush forth from the circuit of sens ory life, and the streams of doctrine that flow across the face of the natural mind and discharge into sens ory knowledge, and the tru ths that descend from above like rain, and all the waste and renewal that comes down into it — that the sensory mind with its self hood should serve as a hos tel and gathering place for all of these , receiving everything into itself.

---

**¶12. ** As for all the Divine power and life that descends into the sensory mind, and the vital breath that the selfhood draws into itself — by which it distur bs the whole body of sensory knowledge — * [ the text becomes fragmentary here ; what can be read suggests :] * a fullness ar ises between the movement of the prop rium and the ongoing work of purification, but the sensory mind itself … * [the remainder is lost and res ists confident translation ].*

reconstructions.reconstructed_text: After the Living Spirit constructed things and the worlds, he came up and set himself upon this earth. He gave a sign to the King of Glory, who turned the three wheels and caused the wheels that are found [in the sphere to extend] up above all the mountains; he spread forth the wind to them, he breathed on them, he stirred them up, he washed the earth with the waters. And the waste and the accretion of the three vessels, they of water and of darkness and of fire, which had been discharged upon the earth, he gathered them and deposited them in the sea that is within the walls and the vessels; because of this sea waters are salty. For they have received salt and bitterness from the washing out and cleansing of the three vessels.

The sea giant had stamped upon him the seal of the seconds and the hours, the seal of the days and months and years, the impression of the stars and the signs of the zodiac [and the whole turning of the sphere.] He came into existence from them and was discharged from their power and cast into the sea. The images and the seals and aspects and doctrines and counsels of [the sphere and all its powers] were sealed upon the body of that giant, because he is the residue of them all. Consequently, each star that will shine, and each sign of the zodiac that will turn: of one he shall be its inducement, and of another its confirmation.
This is also the case with the sea giant, who too was moulded and sculpted by the power of the lust inside him from many doctrines and counsels that belong to the residue of the wheel of the sphere.
The archetype of the giant was constructed for three things.

The first: That the sphere would be relieved and purified of the burden present in it. In the same way that the ten firmaments were purified and relieved of the burden of the three vessels; so was it also done to the sphere, that it too might be relieved and purified of the burden and the waste inside it.

The second: That he might add a [fetter] and a prison to the wheel and the signs of the zodiac that are bound to it, so that when they wish to go up above, you can find the sea giant dragging them back as by an iron [chain], and they are unable to go up; and when the powers of the wheel would take a decision on a guileful thing, and it enters their mind to come down to the earth, they are not able to descend because of this stake that is nailed to the wheel upon the [foundation] of the firmaments. This is one. However, this other one, because of its sleepless watchers that are set over it, it is turned all the time.

The third thing: That the wind and the water and the fire that gush from the circuit of the sea, and the rivers that flow upon the face of the earth discharging into the sea, and the rainwaters that come to ground, and the waste and rebirth that come down to it; that sea will be a hostel and gathering place for all of these.

As for all the power and the life that comes down to the sea, and in the breath that the sea giant will breathe and draw it into him that he might disturb the sea[, there arises a] fullness and a [stirring that] becomes between his movement [and the powers that would] purify; but the sea [...]

This matter is comparable with a craftsman who might take the stamped impressions of many coins and cast them on the fire, and mould them [to a single] image. These thousands of impressions and thousands of shapes [are perfected] and make a single body [and one likeness from them all.]

He was discharged into the sea like this, the way a cloud might discharge rainwater into the midst of the sea. They compelled him totally through the action of the power and the helmsmanship of the angels. He was swept down to the mill, the place where he was constructed in the setting up of the universe; and the sea also conceived him [in its depths;] for its part [it moulded him, ] it being his chief sculptor and chief craftsman. It sculpted him in a likeness, he being changed more than the other residue of the sea bodies.

When the Father of Life came, rising in his ascent to the heights, he discharged the wheel of the stars; he washed it out and loosened all the sediment that was in it. He cast it down to this great inner sea like [ ... ] of the mountain. And that waste, the sediment of the washing out of the wheel, he cast it down and mixed it in with the sea waters. Its own thought collected it together; and the thought gathered the waste together in this way. It made it fast and fixed it [ ... ]
